subject: RFP: Capacity matrix & SKU fallback planning for Dedicated Pool
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: sana.rizvi@acme.ai, procurement@acme.ai
Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme RFP: Dedicated capacity sizing questions

Jonas —

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is the short questionnaire for capacity planning (we capped it to the most important fields). High level context: we run a mixture of chat and long-form generation models. Peak concurrency is often around 650 concurrent sessions with typical 80-token requests and occasional sampling for longer assists (up to 2k tokens). We want reserved capacity for our US production traffic with burst to handle major campaign spikes.

Key asks:
- Can you map recommended GPU SKUs to our stated throughput targets?
- What burst lanes do you support and how are they priced?
- How would you handle automated fallback to cheaper SKUs when reserved pool saturates?

Attaching the questionnaire: 20260517-acme-rfp-questions.pdf

Appreciate a reply with a worked example and an approximate cost delta between H100/H16/L4 options.

Thanks,
Liam O'Neill
Head of Procurement, Acme AI
procurement@acme.ai
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, sana.rizvi@acme.ai
Date: 2026-05-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme RFP: Dedicated capacity sizing questions

Liam —

Thanks for the questionnaire, got it. We're preparing a short worked example and a capacity matrix that maps GPU SKUs, reserved concurrency, and expected throughput per-second for the common workload profiles you outlined (chat 80t, generation 2kt peak).

High level plan:
- We'll run two baseline reserved pool proposals: (A) performance-lean (H100 primary + small H16 overflow) and (B) cost-lean (A10G/L4 blend with H16 buffer).
- Each proposal will include: reserved GPU counts, expected token throughput (tokens/sec), client-visible tail latency at 95/99 percentile, and an explicit burst/fallback policy with pricing impact.
- We'll include a fallback policy that prefers quantized L4 instances for low-priority workloads and keeps strict SLOs for core flows.

Expect our detailed matrix and the XLSX workbook by end of day tomorrow. Looping in Kim for kernel-fitment/quantization notes and Karthik for contractual burst terms.

Jonas Weber
Senior Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-18T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity matrix draft + assumptions

Jonas / team —

I've attached the capacity workbook (20260518-rw-inference-capacity-matrix.xlsx). Key assumptions encoded in the sheet: 1) baseline model is a 13B chat model (fp16, kernel-optimized) and 2) long-form generation uses a 34B variant with KV cache warming.

Quick highlights from sheet:
- H100 (full precision) estimate: 1 H100 -> ~9200 tokens/sec for chat-80t flows, baseline 95p latency ~120ms at 20 concurrent sessions.
- H16 (mixed) estimate: 1 H16 -> ~4200 tokens/sec for same profile, good price/perf for mid-tier.
- A10G/L4 (quantized) estimate: 1 L4 -> ~1500 tokens/sec (quantized model), best cost for non-latency-critical batch workloads.

Fallback logic proposed (in plain language):
- Primary reserved pool serves core routes pinned to H100/H16.
- When reserved pool saturation reaches 85% for sustained 60s, new low-priority requests are routed to the cost-lean L4 pool with a token-cost multiplier.
- For non-critical evaluation workloads, prefer A10G/L4 from the start.

I've added a 'burst lanes' tab with two options: temporary burst on same GPU family (fast warm-up, higher cost per token) and cross-family overflow with lower performance variance but cheaper unit cost.

Attachments: 20260518-rw-inference-capacity-matrix.xlsx

Kim Park
Sr. Inference Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
From: Sana Rizvi <sana.rizvi@acme.ai>

Cc: liam.oneill@acme.ai, procurement@acme.ai
Date: 2026-05-18T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme RFP: Capacity matrix & SKU fallback planning

Thanks — couple clarifying questions after reading the draft matrix: 
1) For our 650 concurrent sessions baseline, can you show a worked table that maps number of GPUs -> projected sustained throughput -> projected 95p latency?
2) How do you price the burst lanes: flat hourly surcharge vs token surcharge? We want predictability for budgeting.
3) What is the SLA/commitment if overflow hits cheaper SKUs — do you maintain response correctness (sampling/temperature parity) or are there model quality regressions?

One other ask: our security team insists on explicit mention of KV cache isolation and event logging for fallback routes (we need audit evidence for any automatic routing that changes model family).

Sana
Site Reliability Lead, Acme AI
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sana Rizvi <sana.rizvi@acme.ai>, liam.oneill@acme.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-19T10:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme RFP: Capacity matrix & SKU fallback planning

Sana / Liam —

Answers inline and attached a short slide (sku-fallback-chart.png) that summarizes the tradeoffs. See attached and notes below.

1) Worked table (excerpt):
- 650 concurrent chat-80t sessions, target 95p latency <200ms: H100-only reserved pool -> ~8 H100 GPUs (sustained ~73k tokens/sec).
- H16-primary hybrid: ~18 H16 GPUs (sustained ~75k tokens/sec) with slightly higher variance at tail but lower cost.
- Cost-lean L4 blend for same sustained throughput: ~48 L4 instances (quantized) but 95p latency degrades to ~320ms.

2) Burst pricing recommendations:
- Option A (predictable): monthly reserved + flat hourly burst rate (per-GPU-hour) for same family; good for budgeting.
- Option B (usage-aligned): token surcharge for cross-family overflow (per-1k tokens) — better reflects unit economics if you expect low-frequency high-volume spikes.

We recommend Option A for Acme if budgeting predictability is a priority; we show approximate hourly burst rates in the attached workbook.

3) Model quality / correctness:
- We preserve deterministic sampling seeds where possible but quantization and kernel differences can introduce micro-variance in sampling (temperature/entropy behavior). For core routes we recommend pinning model variants to the same family; fallback should be used for non-SLO-critical workloads.

Security / logging:
- KV cache isolation: fallback routes are executed in separate tenant-scoped caches and never share KV state across families.
- Audit logging: every automatic route decision is logged with pre/post state (route decision id, reason code, source IP, timestamp) and exposed via the Console audit API and optional S3 export.

Next steps: I will attach the numeric matrix (XLSX) and the PNG summary. If this looks good, Kim and I can prepare a formal SOW pricing page and a small SLA addendum for overflow behavior.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.ai>

Cc: sana.rizvi@acme.ai, procurement@acme.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Jonas / Kim / Marissa —

This is exactly the level of detail we needed. Two quick asks before we mark this section as closed in the RFP: 1) can you include the explicit hourly burst rates in the XLSX as a single summary tab (we'll attach to procurement docs), and 2) can Marissa provide a short paragraph describing the contractual wording for overflow SLA (we want explicit language to include in our procurement redlines).

If you can get both by EOD Monday, we'll slot Redwood to the shortlist.

Thanks,
Liam
